newsitem.title: UK: Dlr/mark below 40-mth peaks below 1.75 in Europe.
newsitem.headline: Dlr/mark below 40-mth peaks below 1.75 in Europe.

text.p: The dollar bounced over a pfennig from lows to 40-month peaks shy of 1.75 marks at midday Europe, drawing strength from renewed jitters over European monetary union and sterling's rally to five-year highs against the mark.
"We are continuing to see this structural desire to shift out of core EMU currencies into alternatives," said Shean Shepley, international economist at CS First Boston.

The dollar was also seen harnessing strength ahead of the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting on Tuesday and Wednesday, though a rate change is not expected. But traders said the dollar could drift if the FOMC leaves rates steady.

At 1050 GMT, dollar/mark stood at 1.7445/50 vs 1.7381/86 in late Europe on Friday and just below 40-month highs of 1.7465 marks hit in Europe. Dollar/yen was steady to a touch weaker in Europe, trading at 114.46 yen against 114.60/70 yen.

Shepley said with shifts out of core EMU currencies the dollar will continue to attract flows. "Europe has big problems to get over, and the way the politicians are going about it is not very constructive," he added.
EMU jitters resurfaced after a rift within Chancellor Helmut Kohl's ruling alliance over EMU widened Saturday when one of his partners raised the prospect of leaving the coalition.
The row pits members of Kohl's Christian Democratic Union (CDU) against its Bavarian sister party, the Christian Social Union (CSU), and above all Bavarian premier Edmund Stoiber.

Stoiber is calling for a delay in monetary union if the entry criteria are weakened. He has threatened to block German membership of monetary union in the upper house unless the criteria are strictly met.

"Dollar/mark was hit by speculative buying, taking out stops above 1.7425 marks and pushing dollar/mark higher. Also, those awaiting the FOMC tomorrow don't want to put on any fresh positions," said a senior trader at a UK bank.
"But the way the dollar is going some may have to cover their shorts," added the trader.
The U.S. unit should remain well supported ahead of the FOMC and a raft of U.S. economic data later on Monday.
"The markets are awaiting the FOMC meeting, but markets have already priced in no interest-rate change," said Nick Shamin, currency analyst at ANZ Investment.

US May personal income and personal spending, forecast to rise by 0.4 percent and 0.3 percent, respectively, are due at 1230 GMT while new home sales for June, forecast at 786,000, and May Chicago PMI are due at 1400 GMT.
The Chicago PMI index is forecast to rise to 57.5 from 56.8 previously.
Elsewhere, the mark lost its shine against most crosses and the Italian lira after Italy cut its discount and Lombard rates to 6.25 and 7.75 percent, respectively, late on Friday.
Italian treasury minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi said the rate cut brings Italian EMU membership closer but warned against over-optimism.
Sterling/mark pushed to five-year highs above 2.90 marks in Europe, while its trade-weighted index jumped to 102.2 - its highest since April 1991.
